text: Why does ARP have no authentication?
choices: It was designed in 1982 for a network of mutually trusting research institutions, where it was a reasonable assumption
Authentication would make it too slow
It does have authentication, which is usually disabled
explanation: RFC 826 is four pages long and works. Any station may reply to any request and any station may send an unsolicited reply that receivers cache — which is the basis of ARP spoofing today. The mitigations, Dynamic ARP Inspection and DHCP snooping, are add-ons rather than protocol features.
